[quote=qianxun;60437578][spoiler][b]Operation Haiyan[/b]

The departure of the isolationist navy would prove to pose somewhat of an issue against Qianxun forces. Since the start of the operation, Qianxun forces have largely limited their naval capabilities to three types of watercraft: A dozen auxiliary surface combat and landing ships created from converted merchant vessels, which had only some basic armaments like twin 25mm/80 guns and a few anti-ship missile launchers; Five [i]Anlan[/i]-class missile boats, which were airlifted from the Qianxun Lakes with the latest in subsonic anti-ship cruise missile technology, MANPAD missiles, and 30mm guns; and last but not least, three amphibious assault ships supplied courtest of SummitONE, the QNS [i]Du Jiao[/i], QNS [i]Tongyi[/i], and QNS [i]Weizhu[/i]. 

Additionally, an experimental fast combat support ship called the [i]Bicang[/i] ("Jade Repository") would be apparently present among Qianxun naval forces, having been spotted by Astaniran locals due to its unusual design and its many, many missions resupplying the Qianxun expeditionary fleet. However, it has been mysteriously absent since the deposition of the Arono government, possibly having been hidden by Qianxun agents at [i]Kuangye Point[/i], the codename for David Cyriacus's [i]ad hoc[/i] central headquarters.

Qianxun forces had no submarines available in Astanir, having initially thought them to be impractical due to the modernized ASW capabilities of the [i]Anlan[/i]-class. However, with doubts now being spread among Pax Int'l's leadership of the effectiveness of their offensives, the order would be given to retain all twenty Qianxun vessels near the Democratic coast under the protection of its coastal batteries. This move, while criticized by some officials for vastly overestimating the capabilities of the isolationist naval force, would nevertheless be accepted without further incident. Admiral Yun Caibo, the [i]de facto[/i] head of all naval forces and architect of this defensive strategy, would in the mean time order retraining to begin on all available Astaniran Democratic naval ships, with Yun hoping to find a few submarines in the Democratic arsenal which might be used to confront the enemy at the sea.

In the mean time, however, with the Tiansheng pocket now resolved and with General Bai He's 5th Maneuver Army having stalled on the frontline, the time was now for the  1st and 2nd Maneuver Armies of SummitONE operational managers Freya Moran and Edwin Roylance to make their appearance. Unlike Bai He's forces, which were predominantly Astaniran,  1st and 2nd Maneuver Armies would be predominatly Vespurian and Qianxun. Well-armed, well-supplied, and well-trained, though in need of experience in the complex Astaniran jungle terrain, Moran and Roylance would launch a gigantic, "hail army" combined arms charge along the western and central salients formed by Bai's offensives.

Anticipating zealous resistance, Moran and Roylance would both organized DEAD campaigns so that Democratic air forces could work in tandem with the Moran-Roylance offensive. During this time, nearly 40% of all Wuying-98 sorties would be identify and destroy isolationist AA units and radar equipment. The antiquated isolationist strategic bombers sent to blunt Pax Int'l forces would have some trouble reaching their targets thanks to interception by Wuying-89s, chiefly due to the weaker capabilities of the bombers' isolationist escorts, but also thanks to Democratic aerial superiority that had been established against the isolationists since the deposition of Haru Arono. 

To maintain tactical cohesion, exhausted and demoralized troops at the very front of the campaign would start to finally be rotated out in favor of elements of Erzhu Qingsheng's 6th Maneuver Army and the fresh Democratic Legionnaires. Additionally, Democratic forces would also begin advising several "peasant warlords" along their offensive campaign to begin setting up soviets with which to facilitate the construction of supply depots, refueling stations, fresh roads, field hospitals and [i]ad hoc[/i] factories to keep advancing Democratic forces well-supplied. 

[b]Operation Julong[/b]

After negotiating a ceasefire with the Argossian militias, Generals Duan Liqin and Tazio Diodati would be remain content with maintaining a stalemate against the restorationists, with this having been their duty in the first place. While some elements within the 3rd and 4th Maneuver Armies would suggest taking the initiative and instigating a dedicated offensive, both generals would opt against this, fearing both court martial by the CEDC and the risk of opening up a second, far more dangerous front. For now, Operation Julong would restrain itself to just a few infantry skirmishes and minor SEAD raids to keep the restorationists on high alert while also dissuading any attempts at an enemy offensive.

6th Maneuver Army under General Bai He had been initially considered in aiding Julong, though he had instead been reassigned to Operation Haiyan. Without any independent capacity to wage an offensive campaign on their own, Duan and Diodati would diversify their own duties and become diplomats as well, attempting to open up talks with the Sui-mana of Kuhaw-Astan. In their several communiques, the generals would claim to the tribals that their delegations from Teremok had been seized by the Pantagruelis, who were now intent on intervening in the civil war against them, with Gen. Diodati in particular submitting several printed news reports detailing recent atrocities in the southern group of islands.

In the hope of achieving a common platform, the two generals would ask the Sui-mana for a "united front", a temporary alliance so that the matter of the restorationists and isolationists could be resolved. At the end of this campaign, the generals would pledge to honor their contributions to a Democratic Astanir and would propose the possibilities of a two-state solution, with Kuhaw-Astan envisioned as an autonomous state under the Democratic political framework.

[b][url=https://www.nationstates.net/nation=democratic_sanguivallis]Sanguinian[/url] intervention in the Astaniran Civil War[/b]

Following the conclusion of the First Conference of Discussions at the Socialist International, Sanguivallis's geopolitical position had been somewhat improved. EDU had formed a gargantuan economic blockade of the Sanguinian state, though by the time of the Conference, these economic sanctions had been effectively superseded by the revitalization of Sanguinian economic interests elsewhere, namely in Vespuria and Qianxun. Still, as the second-most important socialist state within the International, the Sanguinan government now resolved itself to protect the communist revolution everywhere, both as a matter of ideological principle and to encourage further Qianxun investments into its slowly recovering economy.

After a brief meeting of the Patriciate, Pio Graci would authorize the creation of a "Shamatine Assault Flotilla" to be placed under the command of his younger brother, Senator Caio Graci. In total, this flotilla consisted of the following vessels:

[list]

[b]Shamatine Assault Flotilla[/b]

SNS [i]Civitas Dei [/i]aircraft carrier
SNS [i]Gloriosus [/i]amphibious transport dock
SNS [i]Radiante [/i]guided missile frigate
SNS [i]Instancabile [/i]guided missile frigate
SNS [i]Brela [/i]oceanic patrol vessel
SNS [i]Ezero [/i]oceanic patrol vessel
SNS [i]Chusra [/i]oceanic patrol vessel
SNS [i]Belsasa [/i]replenishment oiler

[/list]

The flagship of the flotilla would be the [i]Civitas Dei [/i] herself, as of last count the most powerful warship directly affiliated with the Socialist International. Caio Graci, after taking over this ship's naval staff from the previous Serenissima leadership, would quickly make adjustments to its aircraft composition. Having been informed by Qianxun that any further transports would be unnecessary, Graci would replace all 11 multirole helicopters in the Civitas Dei's deck, instead filling the ship to the brim with CNI Grifone III multirole fighters. In total, the carrier would be able to fit 25 of these choppers, with 6 spots left for parking.

Of their manpower, the Sanguinians would bring with them four tank battalions comprising of around 3,600 soldiers, 64 SCC-3 main battle tanks, and 110 Grifone tank destroyers. Senator Onorino Sepe, a member of the Social Renaissance Patriciate, would be assigned with managing the land campaign of their planned intervention, with the four battalions to be named the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th Armored International Battalions respectively under the nominal control of the Democratic Legion.

To avoid being intercepted by the Pantagrueli navy en route, Graci would agree with the recommendation of the Patriciate to take the long way through the White Strait and into the Argos Strait, which would be more diplomatically cumbersome but practical, with Graci himself giving a timetable of around three weeks before they'll be able to take part in the war in Astanir. While that is ongoing, troops aboard the Assault Flotilla would be briefed on the exact nature of the intervention plan.

https://i.imgur.com/VdcMO9k.png

Rather than landing on the Democratic side as most Pax International forces have landed, Caio Graci would inform the fleet of Pax Int'l's plan to instead have the Sanguinians make an audacious amphibious landing at Southern Astanir, towards the protruding karst plateau. However, before that could be possible, the Sanguinians would first have to take over the large restorationist island that was blocking the way, along with whatever ships that the restorationists may be holding there.

However, that would be a discussion for another day. For now, as the ships proceed along their long transit to Astanir, Caio Graci would make sure his troops were well-drilled, well-informed of their specific roles for what was to come, and well-prepared for certain death.[/spoiler][/quote]

[b]Operation Haiyan[/b]
On the naval front to the east, the Isolationists would be conservative in their use of their naval assets, now realising that Qianxun is a far more powerful opponent that it first appeared. Initially, only a single submarine and a handful of cruisers would be deployed onto the naval frontlines to test the waters. If this initial test showed Qianxuns naval capabilities to be effective, the Isolationists would begin slowly sending in more ships, attempting to wear down the democratic forces and keep their attention on the naval front, whilst the isolationists prepared for a renewed ground offensive to keep the democrats away from Astan.

On the eastern coast, the isolationists would attempt to make a renewed push against Bais forces. Whilst little progress would be made on the coastline, due to Qianxuns naval supremacy at this point, the Isolationists would try to push the democrats to the very east in hopes of cutting Bais forces off and eventually crushing the exclave, which the offensive would aim to bring into existence. A joint use of brute force and complex Guerilla warfare would be used to constantly keep the democrats on their toes.

Morans offensive would initially be mostly ignored by the isolationists. The direction of the attack appeared to be towards the west, where there is nothing of significance. As such, only a small deployment would face Morans troops, just enough to provide some amount of resistance, but things would go downhill when the direction of the attack shifted to meet up with Roylances troops. The rapid progress being made by Morans troops would allow them to easily meet Roylances troops and the main frontline.

Roylances offensive would face far more initial resistance, as the isolationists put the most forces into defending from Roylances attack. The democrats ability to take out air defences would aid them a lot in the skies, which would remain firmly in their hands for the entire operation, but on the ground they would be more matched. The isolationists would be forced to adopt a strategy of attrition, sending in wave after wave of troops to keep the democrats at bay. Qianxun and the democrats would be able to easily attack Astan from above at this point, but the sheer amount of defences put in place in and around the city would prevent them from reaching the city during this offensive, managing to gain only minor villages and infrastructure on the very outskirts of the urbanised south of Astanir.

Additionally, the isolationists would deploy a small battalion from the rural town of Luwakki, to would launch the Luwakki offensive. This attack would aim to cut the central salient in two, capitalising on the fact that Roylances forces were now mostly located on the southern front, pushing towards Astan. This small battalion would move quietly through the night to avoid being spotted by enemy aircraft, discreetly capturing unguarded transport routes and settlements, eventually regrouping back in isolationist territory on the other side of the central salient. This would now trap Roylances forces in an enclave, which could be slowly occupied through similar tactics as used to split the enemy in half.

[b]Operation Julong[/b]
The restorationists would decide to only delegate enough troops to keep the Democratic frontline stable, instead focusing on attacking the tribes of Kuhaw-Astan to help solidify their northern frontier.

Meanwhile, talks with the Sui-mana would go well for the democrats. The Sui-mana and the rest of the tribes had already been informed of the situation with Pantagruel, which would make Qianxun and the Democratic army appear more legitimate. Therefore, the Sui-mana would accept the proposition of a temporary united front against the threat of the isolationists and restorationists, but would make themselves very clear in the fact that they would not accept a solution where they are any kind of autonomous state. They would insist that any two-state solution wound result in complete Argossian independence, but would also state that this issue could be pushed aside for the time being. Additionally, the sui-mana would invite both democratic and Qianxun representatives to a face-to-face meeting with the tribal leaders of Kuhaw-Astan and representatives of Nordiheim.

[b]Sanguinian intervention[/b]
The Sanguinian would make a grave mistake by deciding that the restorationist stronghold island must be attacked. This island is the primary location where the restorationists keep stocks of food, weapons, ammunition and also where ships and aircraft get deployed from and serviced at, making it the powerhouse behind the restorationist war effort. This island is also heavily defended by anti-air and a large naval presence. The restorationists could never allow this island to be taken over, so they made certain that an attack would almost certainly spell suicide.

Additionally, if an attack were to take place, it would be as loud and obvious as a firework explosion, due to the huge resistance and resulting bloodshed that the Sanguinian would face. This would alert the isolationists and would likely make an invasion of southern Astanir far less feasible. Ultimately, the Sanguinians could really only invade by circumventing the stronghold island, but as the ships slowly made their way towards Astaniran waters, the future would be uncertain
